solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Advance notice: 'No bumping on the 13'?

definitions.meaning: a caution given beforehand so nobody can later claim surprise
a sign forbidding collisions on the dodgem cars at a funfair is a caution posted at the ...

explanation.surface: A puzzling notice: an early announcement that reads like a sign at the bumper cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The 13 is 13-across, DODGEMS, the bumper cars of a funfair, so the quoted sign is literally a warning at the fair. The second reading is cryptic, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a caution given early enough that the person warned has no excuse later.

clue.text: Loudmouth's crazy wish to invade Scottish Kingdom

indicators.note: to invade says the jumbled letters go inside the name of the Scottish region

parts.note: Fife, the region of eastern Scotland traditionally called the Kingdom of Fife

indicators.note: crazy suggests the word wish is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mad desire to conquer part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' makes SHWI, which 'to invade' places inside. Fife, in eastern Scotland, is traditionally called the Kingdom of Fife.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishwife is a coarse, shrill-voiced woman, so a loud, abusive talker; the term comes from women who sold fish in markets.

clue.text: The setter's taking on tricky recce to find dessert

indicators.note: taking on means the setter's phrase takes the jumbled letters into itself

parts.note: the setter is, from the setter's point of view, I am

indicators.note: tricky signals that the letters of recce are to be scrambled

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler undertakes a difficult reconnaissance mission to locate a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is read as 'the setter is', the compiler speaking of himself. 'tricky' makes CECRE, which 'taking on' splits the setter's phrase to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen sweet served as a pudding course.

clue.text: Band in straw hat PC found to be questionable

indicators.note: questionable here means doubtful in arrangement, so the letters of straw hat PC are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A policeman's straw boater seems out of place in a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians to go with the straw hat; it is a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: The strap that holds a wristwatch on is a band of leather or metal.

clue.text: Participants in trial on genetics get together

indicators.note: Participants in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Volunteers in a genetics study are expected to cooperate.
explanation.definitionFit: To get along with someone is to get on with them, so get together amicably.

clue.text: Resort to a crude 'Z' when carving

indicators.note: carving suggests cutting up and reshaping, so the letters of to a crude plus Z are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to cutting a rough letter Z, like Zorro with his sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a verb ('resort to'); it is the noun, the holiday coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Riviera is a famous stretch of Mediterranean holiday resorts.

clue.text: Investigate commotion that has advanced over peninsula

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely
a din is a loud racket
A stands for advanced, as in A level
via means by way of, as a route passes over or through a place

explanation.surface: Look into a disturbance that has spread across a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographically Norway and Sweden occupy a large northern European peninsula bearing this name.

clue.text: Wave mat in a 1ac feature

definitions.note: 1ac with 11ac is FAIR WARNING; the feature here belongs to the fair alone

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy wave rolling to shore
a coaster is a small mat put under a glass

explanation.surface: A wave-patterned mat is a decoration at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: '1ac' points to 1-across, but only its first word FAIR: the ride is a feature of a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic funfair ride of cars on a steep looping track.

clue.text: Capital husband serving community

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A city-dwelling husband is doing good works for the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a local community served by its own church and priest.

clue.text: Race to follow daughter

parts.note: to see is to follow an argument, to understand it
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A runner in a race chases their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a running contest; it is a line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical usage takes seed to mean offspring or descendants, a lineage or people.

clue.text: France welcomes remarkably tall oboe player

indicators.note: welcomes means France takes the rearranged letters in between its two letters
remarkably implies the letters of tall oboe appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: France receives a remarkably tall oboist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges TALL OBOE into OOTBALLE, which 'welcomes' puts between F and R. 'player' suggests the oboist; it is a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer is someone who plays football, a player of the game.

clue.text: See 1
Residents in hospital somewhat nervous? No end!

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a bit means to some extent

indicators.note: No end says the final letter of the word for nervous is cut off

parts.note: antsy means restless or jittery

explanation.surface: Patients in hospital feel rather nervous, endlessly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' looks like the idiom 'very much'; it removes the Y from ANTSY.
explanation.definitionFit: People who live in a place are its inhabitants.

clue.text: Work on diamond treasures for a 1 Across feature

definitions.note: 1 Across with 11 Across is FAIR WARNING; the feature here belongs to the fair alone

parts.note: to do a task is to work on it
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games
gems are precious jewels or prized things

explanation.surface: A jeweller working on a diamond collection.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 Across' points to FAIR, the first word of 1-across: bumper cars are a funfair attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Small electric bumper cars that drivers crash into each other are a staple funfair ride.

clue.text: Speedily kept unharmed by cold in marsh (around zero at first), poor Flora embraces quiet

indicators.note: in says everything else is placed within the word for marsh

parts.note: a fen is low-lying marshland, as in East Anglia

indicators.note: embraces means the shuffled name takes the word for quiet inside it
poor suggests the name Flora is in a sorry, disordered state, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: SH is the call for silence

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of zero

explanation.surface: Poor Flora, stuck in a freezing marsh, is told to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' makes LAFRO, which 'embraces' the quiet call to give LASHFRO; Z from 'zero at first' follows, and all goes 'in' the marsh. 'around' is read as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Food frozen very rapidly keeps its texture and quality, so cold preserves it quickly without damage.

clue.text: Capriciously ordering a flower …

indicators.note: capriciously means on a whim, so the letters of ordering a are set out in a random new order

explanation.surface: Someone whimsically asks for a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means something that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a flower is something that flows, so a river; this one forms much of the US-Mexico border.

clue.text: … flower given to detective novelist, used to a certain extent as sweetener

indicators.note: given to says the bloom is attached after the shortened surname
used to a certain extent means only part of the novelist's surname is used, its tail dropped

parts.note: Colin Dexter wrote the Inspector Morse novels
a rose is a garden flower

explanation.surface: A flower presented to a crime writer, used sparingly as a sugar substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: After 15-down's river, 'flower' here really is a bloom. 'used to a certain extent' trims ER from DEXTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextrose is a form of glucose, a sugar used to sweeten foods.

clue.text: Cover-ups — they're fundamentally on the fiddle

definitions.meaning: skimpy undergarments that cover very little
on a violin the lowest string sounds the note G as its fundamental tone

explanation.surface: Cover-ups whose perpetrators are basically crooks on the fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests cheating; it is literally on a violin. 'Cover-ups' suggests scandal-hiding; here they are scanty briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: These are minimal thong garments, and also the lowest-pitched strings of a violin.

clue.text: Box office in good shape as to prospects for critical appraisals

parts.note: OK means fine or in good condition
re means concerning or as to
views are outlooks or prospects

explanation.surface: Healthy ticket sales bode well for how the critics will judge a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics' assessments of new books are published as reviews.

clue.text: In a particular capacity, one stubborn chap's elevated above Head of House

indicators.note: above in a down clue puts the reversed part higher than the final letter
elevated in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cuss is an awkward or cussed fellow
A means one

indicators.note: Head of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An obstinate man is promoted over the head of his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns A CUSS upside down in this down entry to give ASSUC; 'above' sets it over H, the 'Head of House'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the role or capacity just named, by virtue of being that thing.

clue.text: Let her loose — free kestrel — as attraction at the 1ac

definitions.note: 1ac with 11ac is FAIR WARNING; the attraction belongs to the fair alone

indicators.note: loose implies the letters of let her are freed from their order and rearranged
free suggests the bird's letters are set loose into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A falconer lets a kestrel fly free as a show at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: '1ac' refers to FAIR, the first word of 1-across: this is a funfair ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall spiral slide that riders descend on mats is a traditional funfair attraction.

clue.text: See 20
See 7
Basket case's starting dance

indicators.note: starting takes the first letter of the word case's

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A basket case starts dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basket case' reads as one phrase; split it: 'Basket' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers carry their catch in a wicker basket of this name.

clue.text: Not occupied, aunt needn't fret

indicators.note: fret means to wear away or agitate, so the letters of aunt needn't are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Reassuring an aunt not to worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fret' reads as 'worry'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A property with no tenant living in it is empty, unlet.

clue.text: Perhaps Milligan's to endure

definitions.meaning: Spike Milligan was one of the comedians of the ... Show, so he is an example of a member of that cast

explanation.surface: Is Milligan perhaps going to persevere?
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a classic BBC radio comedy starring Spike Milligan, Peter Sellers and Harry Secombe.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike Milligan was a famous member of that comedy troupe, and to keep going is to continue or endure.

clue.text: With backs to the wall, only just restraining rough seas

indicators.note: restraining means the word for only just holds the scrambled letters inside it

parts.note: hardly means barely or only just

indicators.note: rough describes choppy seas and signals the letters of seas tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors barely holding back a stormy sea, fighting with their backs to the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' makes ASSE, which 'restraining' holds after the first three letters of the word for only just.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under pressure and stressed, acting like someone hard-pressed with no room to retreat.

clue.text: County borders

definitions.meaning: The short form of Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
flower borders in a garden are planted strips

explanation.definitionFit: Bedfordshire's abbreviation is a county name, and garden borders are flower plots.
